thread:
alex: FYI dashboard alarm: tenant X shows ~150 active streams for 12h. They should be idle/closed. Suspect session map leak after proxy reconnections.

maria: Im seeing duplicate resume tokens in traces. Was that sticky-route change last Monday? :confused:

sam: Pasted relevant proxy log excerpt: 

```
2026-03-20T08:11:02Z INFO  socket closed conn=conn-91 sess=s-901
2026-03-20T08:11:03Z DEBUG session_manager: mark_closed sess=s-901
2026-03-20T08:11:03Z WARN  session not gc: sess=s-901 owner=proxy-thread-7
2026-03-20T08:11:14Z INFO  resume request accepted sess=s-901 client=web-72
```

sam: Close then immediate resume accepted for same id. But the earlier session entry never left the in-memory map. When resumed we end up with two entries: one stale with sockets_count=0 but billed, and one active.

jordan: Repro (SSE): open stream -> kill network -> client attempts resume -> server accepts -> old entry remains. Quick script below: 

```
# repro (approx)
node repro.js --open --kill --reconnect --resume-id s-901
```

kelly: Dashboard UX is confusing: active sockets metric uses session map size which includes stale entries. Suggest we split metrics: sessions.total, sessions.active_sockets, sessions.stale. Also add a small "stale detected" badge in the streams view.

alex: Agree. Also need an automatic cleanup path. Can we introduce a soft-evict that marks stale sessions and schedules GC after cooldown, while returning a header to clients to backoff their resume attempt?

maria: We should be careful: if clients resume after soft-evict we must allow recovery. So mark with `evicted_at` but keep short-term tombstone so billing stops. Add telemetry tag to measure resume_after_evicted.

sam: Sketch of change in session_manager: 

```
if s.last_seen + grace < now {
  s.state = "tombstone"
  metrics.incr("sessions.tombstone")
  // no longer count towards billable active map
}
```

sam: Feature-flagged as `session_tombstone_v1`. Will include `X-Session-Tombstoned: ttl=30s,reason=idle_evict` header.

jordan: One worry: many clients will immediately attempt resume which could spike CPU. We should instruct clients to wait using header `Retry-After` semantics and set `cooldown=30s`. Also update the SDKs to respect this header.

kelly: UX: in console rollout controls, add a note for this canary: "tombstone enabled; will show stale vs active; clients get Retry-After header". Also chart: tombstone->resumes over time.

ops-bot: alert created (#stream-stale-sessions) - threshold 10 tombstones/min for a cluster. Playbook attached.

alex: Sam, please add a log event when resume is accepted for a tombstoned id: `RESUME_POST_TOMBSTONE sess=... client=...`. That will help QA quantify how many legitimate reconnects happen.

sam: will add. I'll also tag metric `resumes.post_tombstone`. PR incoming.

maria: I'll run synthetic probes: reconnect after 5s, 15s, 60s to map tolerance. Will post CSV. We need to tune tombstone TTL so we don't break mobile clients that have flaky networks.

jordan: For canary, set tombstone grace 45s and cooldown header 60s. If synthetic shows too many false positives, increase to 120s.

kelly: Dashboard change requests: 1) split sessions.* metrics 2) add badge showing tombstones in last 1h 3) heatmap for tombstone->resume rate 4) annotate billing meter when tombstones are cleared.

alex: I've slack-checked billing: meter counts sockets by session_map.size currently. We need to change billing pipe to count `sessions.billable` which excludes tombstones. Coordinate with billing to watch delta during canary.

ops-bot: deploy started: proxy@canary-tombstone-20260320. Estimated 15m.

sam: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4033 - adds tombstone state, metrics, headers, and feature flag.

maria: early probe summary: 120 tombstones created, 9 resumed within 10s, billing dropped by ~18 sockets after tombstone cleanup. I uploaded CSV. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Observed a small reconnect spike at t+2s after tombstone; probably some clients aren't honoring the Retry-After. We may need to be more conservative or push SDK update.

kelly: For rollout UX, add a console warning about potential reconnect storms and link to SDK patch. Also an option to enable server-side client-coach: when we tombstone, return a small SSE event advising the client to back off (if using SSE).

alex: Thanks. Action items: sam PR + logs/metrics, kelly dashboard changes + console experiment flag, maria probes + CSV, jordan observe reconnect spike & advise cooldown, billing watch. Don't do global rollout until we verify SDK adoption helps. :rocket:
